615	## ZimmTabs keyboard accessibility fix (2026-08-31)
616	
617	Tim reported: pressing Tab inside an open drawer moves between the active tab and the close
618	icon instead of cycling the other tab headers, and asked for Tab-to-move/Enter-to-activate
619	behaviour. Checked this against the actual spec before changing anything (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 +
620	WAI-ARIA APG's Tabs pattern, both fetched live) rather than assuming either the bug report or a
621	"just make it accessible" reflex fix was right:
622	
623	- **WCAG 2.1.1 doesn't mandate Tab-based navigation for a composite widget** — any keyboard
624	  path satisfies it.
625	- **WAI-ARIA's Tabs pattern is explicit**: `Tab` moves focus into/out of the tablist as a whole
626	  (arrives on the active tab, leaves to the next focusable element outside it — the close icon,
627	  here); Left/Right/Home/End move *within* the tablist. Two activation models exist —
628	  **automatic** (arrow keys switch the panel immediately, no Enter needed) is recommended
629	  specifically "when panel content is not costly to display," which is exactly this case
630	  (static content, no fetch). **Manual** (Enter/Space required) is for the opposite case.
631	- `ZimmTabs` already implemented automatic activation with Left/Right and a roving tabIndex —
632	  the reported "bug" was actually the Tab key behaving per spec. Confirmed with Tim to keep
633	  automatic activation and fix the real, separate gap instead: no `aria-controls`/`id` linking
634	  each tab to its panel, so a screen reader couldn't announce what a tab controls.
635	
636	**Fixed:**
637	- `ZimmTabs`: added `Home`/`End` key support (jump to first/last tab); new required `ariaLabel`
638	  prop (the tablist itself needs an accessible name — no visible on-page label exists for it,
639	  per APG) and `idPrefix` prop, each tab now gets `id={idPrefix}-tab-{tab.id}` and
640	  `aria-controls={idPrefix}-panel`.
641	- `ZimmPdpDrawer`: generates `idPrefix` via React's `useId()` (unique even with the boutique
642	  `ZimmDrawer` also mounted on the same page); its panel now has `id={idPrefix}-panel`,
643	  `aria-labelledby` pointing at the *currently active* tab's id (updates on every switch), and
644	  `tabIndex={0}` — the last one is its own separate APG recommendation (a tabpanel needs to be
645	  in the Tab sequence when its content isn't itself reliably focusable), so `Tab` from the
646	  active tab now lands in the panel content before reaching the close icon.

# PR #67 Review — feat(pdp): ZimmDrawer/ZimmTabs/ZimmPdpDrawer + real PDP info-link wiring

**Tooling note up front:** my actual tool list this session is `Read` + `Bash` only — no Task/Agent dispatch tool and no callable Figma/browser tool were present despite an MCP server description appearing in context (it did not correspond to an invokable function). I ran every angle below myself, sequentially, as its own rigorous pass rather than fanning out to sub-agents, and I flag every place that limitation actually bit.

---

## Angle 1 — Correctness/regression + contract fidelity

**🔴 Must-fix — CONFIRMED (via direct source trace, not rendered) — UNIFORM (same bug shape already found+fixed once, missed a second time).**
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/index.tsx` (lines ~62-68) still passes `__css` to `<ModalOverlay>` and `<ModalContent>`:
```
<ModalOverlay __css={{ background: styles.overlay.background, zIndex: styles.overlay.zIndex }} />
<ModalContent ref={setContentNode} __css={{ ...styles.panel, maxWidth, margin: styles.overlay.padding }}>
```
The plan doc (`.docs/temp/SFCC-736-195-drawer-tabs-plan.md`, "Fixed — width-clip + overlay bug") documents finding and fixing this *exact* bug on `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` by switching `__css`→`sx` on `DrawerOverlay`/`DrawerContent`. I traced the actual installed `node_modules/@chakra-ui/modal@2.7.0` source to check whether the fix was needed here too:
- `node_modules/@chakra-ui/modal/dist/drawer.mjs` literally re-exports `ModalOverlay as DrawerOverlay` — it is the **same component**, not a lookalike.
- `DrawerContent` (`chunk-JIPYISAW.mjs`) and `ModalContent` (`chunk-6TYU4DP7.mjs`) share byte-for-byte identical prop-spread order: `{..., ...dialogProps, __css: dialogStyles, children}` — the literal `__css: dialogStyles` sits *after* the spread, so Chakra's own internal style wins and the caller's `__css` (which survives inside `dialogProps.__css` via `getDialogProps`'s passthrough, confirmed in `chunk-XG6IELTC.mjs`) is silently discarded.
- `ModalOverlay` has the opposite collision: `{...motionProps, __css: overlayStyle, ref, className, ...rest}` — `...rest` (carrying the caller's `__css`) is spread *last*, so the caller's value wins outright and **replaces** Chakra's own `position:fixed / inset-equivalent / 100vw / 100vh` defaults entirely (plain object-literal semantics, not a merge).
- `zimmModal.css.ts`'s recipe has real, distinct content (`backgroundColor: var(--zimm-color-bg-07)`, `padding: var(--zimm-scale-3xl)`, no default `maxWidth`), and `theme/index.ts`/`theme/components/index.ts` confirm `theme.components.Modal` is **never set by Zimmermann** — only the separately-named `ZimmModal` key is registered. Since Chakra's own `<ModalContent>` internally resolves styles from `theme.components.Modal` (not `ZimmModal`), the net effect is that the dialog panel would fall back to whatever generic `Modal` theme SFCC's base theme/Chakra ships, not Zimmermann's own panel styling or the caller's `maxWidth` — and the overlay would lose its full-viewport fixed positioning.

This directly contradicts the plan doc's own claim ("the refactored ZimmModal/ZimmSubscribeModal — fully correct... proving the CSS-var/theme pipeline itself works fine") — that conclusion came from an early screenshot glance, not the later dedicated DOM-inspection script that specifically root-caused this exact mechanism for `zimmDrawer`. Neither `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s own story nor `footer/index.stories.tsx`'s `SubscribeModalOpen` story assert on background colour or maxWidth pixel values (I read both), so this could pass every existing automated check while still rendering wrong. **I could not render this in an actual browser** — no browser/screenshot tool was available, and I deliberately avoided writing a throwaway test/script per the "no code" instruction. The object-spread mechanism itself is unambiguous JS semantics applied to the real shipped library code, which is why I'm calling it CONFIRMED rather than PLAUSIBLE, but the ultimate on-screen appearance remains unverified by me directly.

**🟡 Should-fix — PLAUSIBLE (reasoned from React key-reconciliation semantics, not observed) — ONE-OFF.**
`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`:
```
<ZimmPdpDrawer key={activePdpTabId ?? 'closed'} isOpen={isPdpDrawerOpen} onClose={closePdpDrawer} ... />
```
`use-modal-state.ts`'s `onClose` does one combined `setState(prev => ({isOpen:false, data: resetDataOnClose ? null : prev.data}))` (`resetDataOnClose` defaults `true`). So on every close, `isOpen` *and* the key-driving `data` flip together in the same commit — the `key` changes from e.g. `'details-and-care'` to `'closed'` at the exact moment `isOpen` becomes `false`. React treats a changed key as "unmount old instance, mount a fresh one" rather than "re-render this instance with new props," so the old `ZimmPdpDrawer` (and whatever `AnimatePresence`/`Slide` exit machinery Chakra's Drawer uses internally) is torn down immediately instead of being given the `isOpen:false` prop transition it needs to play its slide-out animation. Functionally the drawer still closes; the plausible visible defect is losing the close animation every time. Contrast with `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s own `CloseButtonClosesTheDrawer` story, which doesn't use this key pattern and explicitly waits for the animated removal (`waitForElementToBeRemoved`) — that story would not catch this, since it never exercises the parent's key-remount wiring.

**Confirmed correct, no defect:**
- `ZimmPdpDrawer`'s `initialTabId` fallback (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/index.tsx:41-42`, `tabs.find(...) ?? tabs[0]?.id ?? ''`) is genuinely implemented, and the `InvalidInitialTabIdFallsBackToFirst` story (`index.stories.tsx:146-159`) genuinely asserts `aria-selected='true'`/`tabindex='0'` on the fallback tab — matches the CodeRabbit-round-2 claim exactly.
- `useZimmModal`/`ZimmModal`'s public shape (`isOpen, mounted, onClose, maxWidth, labelledBy, describedBy, children`) is unchanged (diffed directly). `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s own `index.tsx` has **zero diff** in this PR — only its `.stories.tsx` changed — confirming "zero code changes" literally.
- `use-modal-state.ts` is a sound, correctly-typed copy-first override — functional updaters correctly read `prev.data`/`prev.isOpen` where needed, no stale-closure issues.
- `product-view/index.tsx`'s `footerLinks?: React.ReactNode` (default `null`, appended to the object-shaped props type) is genuinely additive — cannot break an existing caller that omits it.

## Angle 2 — Conventions, tier ownership, process

**Testing.md/testing.mdc Portal exception — technically accurate, CONFIRMED.** `.storybook/preview.tsx` configures only `ChakraProvider`/`IntlProvider` decorators, no custom portal container. Chakra's `Drawer` literally wraps `Modal` and reuses `ModalOverlay` (confirmed above), both default-porting to `document.body`. `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s `Large` story genuinely uses `within(document.body)` with an inline citation of the new rule — self-consistent.
